outcome: initiation of breastfeeding in the first hour after delivery
cohort: The study included 4827 women who gave birth in Spain between 2013 and 2018, excluding mothers whose children were admitted to hospital at the time of birth.
finding: A three-variable predictive model (highest number of children, skin-to-skin contact at birth, and dystocic delivery) demonstrated excellent predictive ability for identifying women at high risk of not initiating breastfeeding within the first hour after delivery.
mod_finding: Dystocic delivery was found to reduce the likelihood of the onset of breastfeeding within the first hour after birth.
